details.description: Azure AI Speech's text-to-speech service, part of Microsoft's Azure AI Foundry Tools, converts written text into natural-sounding speech using deep neural networks. It offers more than 500 standard neural voices out of the box across 100+ languages and locales, plus the option to create a custom brand voice from a small set of recordings. It is built for scenarios such as voice assistants, audiobook narration, and in-car navigation.
advantages: Provides more than 500 out-of-the-box standard neural voices across 100+ languages and locales.
Supports full SSML markup to adjust pitch, pauses, pronunciation, rate, and volume, and to mix multiple voices in one document.
Each standard voice model is available at both 24 kHz and high-fidelity 48 kHz sample rates.
A batch synthesis API can asynchronously generate audio longer than 10 minutes, such as audiobooks or lectures, in addition to real-time synthesis.
Viseme events expose facial animation data (lip and jaw position) for lip-sync applications, currently for en-US voices.
disadvantages: Viseme (facial animation) support is currently limited to en-US neural voices.
use_cases: Creating a custom brand voice for a product

notes: This catalog entry (azure/speech/azure-tts) covers Azure's standard (non-HD) neural voices as a group, not one named voice. The source states only a '100+ languages and locales' count, so no per-language list is given per the count-only rule. The '500+ voices' figure is not stated on the text-to-speech overview page itself; it is confirmed on Microsoft's high-definition-voices page, which gives 'More than 500' for non-HD Azure Speech voices in its comparison table, so that page was added to sources.
